knowledge_point.title: Finding Two Scalar Factors in a Linear Combination

question.:question/worked-solution:
![Completed vector path](images/5d/5d7bbadbc141798871c16c1175696cf27628e2966c84d2bb2f744ff65d527c71.png)

Follow the supplied route $O\to A\to C$. On the grid, $OA$ is twice the length of $\mathbf{a}$ and points in the same direction, so $\overrightarrow{OA}=2\mathbf{a}$.

The segment from $A$ to $C$ moves six squares right and three squares down. A copy of $\mathbf{b}$ moves two squares right and one square down. Thus $AC=3|\mathbf{b}|$, with the same direction, and $\overrightarrow{AC}=3\mathbf{b}$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AC}\\
&=2\mathbf{a}+3\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, their coefficients are unique. Matching coefficients gives $\lambda=2$ and $\mu=3$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding Two Scalar Factors in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
![](images/99/992be4e67316804381ffc38860d2eaf23fd4a93cfe22ec4918c30c41e34ade57.png)

Consider the picture above. If $\mathbf{t}=\lambda \mathbf{r}+\mu \mathbf{s}$, then$\,\lambda =$

$-\frac{1}{2}$

and 
$\mu =$

$-\frac{5}{2}$

.
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/c0/c0f7f4df52373ca602aff41c97a5b8413f510353874540b76147c527a2f4b18c.png)

In $△ORT$ shown above, we have:

- $OR=\frac{1}{2}|\mathbf{r}|$

- $\overset{\to }{OR}$ has the opposite direction to $\mathbf{r}$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OR}=-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{r}.$

Similarly:

- $RT=\frac{5}{2}|\mathbf{s}|$

- $\overset{\to }{RT}$ has the opposite direction to $\mathbf{s}$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{RT}=-\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{s}.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf{t} & =\overset{\to }{OR}+\overset{\to }{RT} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{r}-\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $$
\displaystyle \mathbf{t}=\lambda \mathbf{r}+\mu \mathbf{s}=-\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{r}-\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{s}.
$$ 

Since $\mathbf{s}∦\mathbf{r},$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-\frac{1}{2}$ and $\mu =-\frac{5}{2}$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing a Vector That Satisfies a Ratio in Terms of Known Vectors

question.:question/problem:
![](images/6a/6a25f87080a52c536be8a179cf922bfddf0608a6d3933a6e99cb4b88a3babcf6.png)

In the diagram, $X$ lies on the segment $AB$. The given vectors are $\overrightarrow{OA}=a$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}=b$. The lengths satisfy $AX:XB=1:2$.

Use the path
$$
\overrightarrow{OX}=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AX}
$$
and the given relation $\overrightarrow{AB}=b-a$ to find $\overrightarrow{OX}$ in terms of $a$ and $b$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The ratio $AX:XB=1:2$ splits $AB$ into $1+2=3$ equal parts. Since $\overrightarrow{AX}$ points from $A$ toward $B$,
$$
\overrightarrow{AX}=\frac{1}{3}\overrightarrow{AB}=\frac{1}{3}(b-a).
$$
Following the supplied path gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OX}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AX}\\
&=a+\frac{1}{3}(b-a)\\
&=\frac{2}{3}a+\frac{1}{3}b.
\end{aligned}
$$
The larger coefficient belongs to $a$: $X$ is closer to $A$ than to $B$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Solid grid lines are one unit apart; dotted lines divide each square in half.

![](images/3f/3f3d535d41f1efaf3cd1ab6af134c8264583281d49007aa1d272b84c5f04fe6c.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\lambda\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{5}{2}\,(-3, 2)=\left(-\frac{15}{2}, 5\right). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(-4, 4).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/5d/5d25ca9ee6973a180e4aa36d516544c9f2e1f42c38a44b9c037e9dc4829ceedc.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{b}$, whose grid displacement is $(-4, 4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{-4}{-4}=1 \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{4}{4}=1
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{b}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\mathbf{b}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \\
&=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=1$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Solid grid lines are one unit apart; dotted lines divide each square in half.

![](images/df/dfb02e1d9202130f955625a46621b81e8fdb9ff6c7f66e183577eb13e2ad2775.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\lambda\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{5}{2}\,(-2, 3)=\left(-5, \frac{15}{2}\right). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(-7, 7).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/ae/ae434599433e3432485a0a5d2d410c20d7a13e0d16847cb5a6c7f281587e03b2.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{b}$, whose grid displacement is $(-4, 4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{-7}{-4}=\frac{7}{4} \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{7}{4}=\frac{7}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{b}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\frac{7}{4}\mathbf{b}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{7}{4}\mathbf{b} \\
&=\frac{5}{2}\mathbf{a}+\frac{7}{4}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=\frac{7}{4}$.

knowledge_point.title: Finding a Scalar Factor When Direction Reverses

question.:question/problem:
The three vectors share an origin, and each grid square has the same side length.

![](images/07/072fdd66978bd3d1c50b6979c4e5fbcf63bdd01b16e06b1cfb325e41d706c2cf.png)

Given $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+4\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
First trace $4\mathbf{b}$ from the common origin $O$ to a point $P$: keep its direction and scale its length. The remaining path from $P$ to the endpoint $C$ must be the unknown multiple of $\mathbf{a}$.

![](images/38/388f5ac51d455964d4e91e103e6760f097214a0eac64b9296418c14513fd9245.png)

Following the grid direction of $\mathbf{a}$ takes $2$ steps, while the parallel path $PC$ has $6$ steps. Their length ratio is $\frac{6}{2}=3$. The remaining path points in the opposite direction to $\mathbf{a}$, so
$$
\overrightarrow{PC}=-3\mathbf{a}.
$$
Adding the path vectors gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC}\\
&=4\mathbf{b}+(-3\mathbf{a})\\
&=-3\mathbf{a}+4\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are nonparallel, these coefficients are unique. Comparing with $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+4\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=-3$. The minus sign records the reversed direction.
